text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The privatisation of a cement factory was broadcast live on television for the first time.
- Justice Minister Sevket Kazan says a gangster at the centre of a security scandal, Abdullah Catli, killed a leading casino owner in July.
- The head of the anti-terror unit in Turkey's intelligence service tells parliamentary commission probing the scandal that Catli worked abroad for their organisation after 1980.
- The Islamist-led government approves a a five-day holiday, including the weekend, for New Year.
- MPs from the junior coalition partner True Path Party hint at quitting because the party is involved in the security scandal.
- More than 5,000 workers end a four-day strike at oil refiner Petkim.
- Electricity bills expected to rise as private companies have to pay the state for the right to produce and distribute electricity.
- Interior minister suspends seven policemen for being involved in a security scandal.
